about: The clauses, inferences and spec conflicts the ACDC cases cite, from the ACDC specification v1.0 (tag v1.0, commit 4a543c549fd9811c23bf97b0daaf48400f4005c2, spec/spec-body.md), and, where a clause names spec "cesr", from the CESR specification v1.0 (tag v1.0, commit 037129608b9e6960858b752019ac273d40d7386c). Each quote must appear verbatim exactly once in its pinned text, under the named heading; a clause's quote must contain its level's keyword. Inferences and conflicts quote the ACDC text, and an inference is used only with a clause from the ACDC text. The generator checks all of this before it writes a case.

a-and-A.quote: An ACDC MUST not have both a non-empty `a` field value and a non-empty `A` field value (see next section) when it has either.

blid.quote: The blinding SAID, BLID, `b` field value MUST be calculated as a cryptographic strength digest on the CESR serialization of the concatenation of block field values.

blinded-attachment.quote: It MAY be provided as an attachment to some message, such as the associate ACDC, as part of a CESR serialization that MUST use one of the CESR group or count codes labeled `BlindedStateQuadruples` with code format `-a##` or `BigBlindedStateQuadruples` with code format `--a######`.

edge-far.quote: In order for a given Edge to be valid, at the very least, a Validator MUST confirm that the SAID of the provided far node ACDC matches the node, `n` field value given in the near node ACDC Edge block and MUST confirm that the provided far node ACDC satisfies its own schema.

edge-i2i.quote: The `I2I` unary operator, when present, means that the Issuer AID of the current ACDC in which the Edge resides MUST be the Issuee AID of the node to which the Edge points. Therefore, to be valid, the ACDC node pointed to by this Edge MUST be a Targeted ACDC.

edge-schema.quote: The far node ACDC MUST also validate against an Edge block's schema, `s` field when present.

field-order.quote: When present, the top-level fields MUST appear in the following order: `[v, t, d, u, i, rd, s, a, A, e, r]`.

key-state.quote: The verifiable key state for AIDs MUST be established with the KERI protocol [[2](#KERI)].

registry-anchored.section: Binding to Key State at Time of ACDC State Change
registry-anchored.quote: The SAID of this event MUST be anchored in the Issuer's KEL as the Registry proof seal.

registry-issuer.quote: The Issuer, `i` field value MUST be the AID of the Issuer.

registry-prior.quote: The prior event SAID, `p` field value MUST be the SAID, `d` field value of the immediately prior event in the TEL.

registry-sn.quote: The sequence number, `n` field value MUST be a hex-encoded string with no leading zeros of a zero-based strictly monotonically increasing integer.

required-fields.quote: The following fields are REQUIRED `[v, d, i, s]` i.e. they MUST appear in any ACDC (not to be confused with other message types in the ACDC protocol).

said-verify.quote: The SAID verification protocol MUST be implemented as follows:

schema-dialect.quote: A mismatch between the supported tooling code dialect version and the `$schema` string value SHOULD cause the validation to fail.

schema-enforced.quote: The compliance of the provided non-schema attribute, `a`, edge, `e`, and rule, `r`, sections MUST be enforced by validating against the composed Schema.

schema-nonlocal.quote: ACDC Sub-Schema indicated by non-local URI references (`$id` or `$ref`) MUST NOT be used because they are not cryptographically end-verifiable.

schema-said.quote: Nonetheless, the provided schema, whether self-contained, attached, or cached MUST validate as a SAD against its provided SAID.

schema-variant.quote: The provided ACDC MUST validate against an allowed combination of the composed variants.

schema-version.quote: Therefore, a given ACDC SHOULD properly pass the JSON Schema validation process regardless of the value of its schema `version` field.

selective-support.quote: To clarify, not all instances of an ACDC MUST employ the minimal Selective Disclosure mechanisms as described herein but all ACDC implementations MUST support any instance of an ACDC that employs the minimal Selective Disclosure mechanisms as described above.

update-anchored.section: Binding to Key State at Time of ACDC State Change
update-anchored.quote: Update events in the Registry's TEL MUST also be anchored.

version-protocol.quote: The protocol field, `PPPP` value in the Version String MUST be `ACDC` for the ACDC protocol.

blid-analogy.quote: A BLID is effectively a type of SAID.
blid-analogy.inference: The text makes a BLID a SAID only by analogy, and its computation "follows the SAID protocol, adapted for fixed-field representations" (line 2141), so the validator obligation CESR line 1194 states for a SAID reaches a BLID only by inference: a block that does not verify against its BLID, or whose BLID is not the update's b, should leave the state unknown, graded SHOULD (generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md, A-G8).

commitment.section: Binding to Key State at Time of ACDC State Change
commitment.quote: To protect against later forgery in the event of a future compromise of the Issuer's signing keys, the Issuer must anchor an *issuance* proof digest seal to the ACDC in its KEL either directly or indirectly.
commitment.inference: This sentence, which says how an ACDC is bound to its issuer's key state, has no keyword, and line 1673 adds that ACDCs "are not directly signed by the Issuer" but bound to the issuer's key state, which line 95 requires a validator to establish by KERI. A seal of the ACDC's most compact SAID on the trunk of that key state is therefore the only issuer commitment the normative text describes, but no keyword sentence obliges a validator to refuse an ACDC without one, so refusing it is inferred and graded SHOULD (generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md, A-G1). The keyworded line 1843 is not cited, because it sits in the IPEX section, which line 1797 declares non-normative.

commitment-registry.section: Binding to Key State at Time of ACDC State Change
commitment-registry.quote: This binds the state of that ACDC to the Issuer's Key State at the time of the update event in the TEL.
commitment-registry.inference: An ACDC that names a registry is bound to its issuer's key state through an anchored update of that registry that includes its SAID; the registry inception names no ACDC. Line 1669's MUSTs bind the issuer that anchors the updates, and no keyword sentence obliges a validator to refuse an ACDC that no anchored update names, so refusing it is inferred and graded SHOULD (generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md, A-G1).

issuer-kel.quote: The verifiable key state for AIDs MUST be established with the KERI protocol [[2](#KERI)].
issuer-kel.inference: The issuer's key state matters to an ACDC only through the issuer's commitment, and no keyword sentence obliges a validator to refuse an uncommitted ACDC (A-G1), so refusing an ACDC whose issuer's key state cannot be established is inferred and graded SHOULD.

liveness.quote: The compliance of the provided non-schema attribute, `a`, edge, `e`, and rule, `r`, sections MUST be enforced by validating against the composed Schema.
liveness.inference: The sentence says what a validator must check, not that it must accept an ACDC that passes. No sentence obliges a validator to accept anything, so that it should report a sound ACDC valid is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, ACDC, Verdicts).

liveness-edge.quote: In order for a given Edge to be valid, at the very least, a Validator MUST confirm that the SAID of the provided far node ACDC matches the node, `n` field value given in the near node ACDC Edge block and MUST confirm that the provided far node ACDC satisfies its own schema.
liveness-edge.inference: The sentence says what a validator must confirm before an edge is valid, not that it must report an edge that passes. That a validator should report each edge it evaluated, and find a sound edge valid, is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, ACDC, Edges).

liveness-registry.section: Binding to Key State at Time of ACDC State Change
liveness-registry.quote: The SAID of this event MUST be anchored in the Issuer's KEL as the Registry proof seal.
liveness-registry.inference: The sentence says what an issuer must anchor, not that a validator must report the registry it finds. That a validator should report the verified head of a sound registry is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, ACDC, Registry state).

producer-a-and-A.quote: An ACDC MUST not have both a non-empty `a` field value and a non-empty `A` field value (see next section) when it has either.
producer-a-and-A.inference: The sentence describes what an issuer emits; it binds the producer, not a validator (docs/design.md, "How levels are derived"), so that a validator should refuse a message that breaks it is inferred and graded SHOULD, and the gap is raised in generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md.

producer-nonlocal.inference: The sentence binds schema authors; it is not addressed to a validator (docs/design.md, "How levels are derived"), so that a validator should refuse a message that breaks it is inferred and graded SHOULD, and the gap is raised in generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md.

producer-order.inference: The sentence describes what an issuer emits; it binds the producer, not a validator (docs/design.md, "How levels are derived"), so that a validator should refuse a message that breaks it is inferred and graded SHOULD, and the gap is raised in generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md.

producer-registry-anchored.inference: The sentence binds the issuer that keeps the registry; it binds the producer, not a validator (docs/design.md, "How levels are derived"), so that a validator should not count a registry whose inception breaks it is inferred and graded SHOULD, and the gap is raised in generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md.

reading-aggregate.quote: This list is then serialized as a list in whatever serialization kind is used by the enclosing ACDC (CESR, JSON, CBOR, MGPK).
reading-aggregate.inference: Neither this sentence nor line 110 has a keyword, and they describe different pre-images for the aggregate. The worked example at lines 951 to 956 settles JSON: its pre-image is the serialized list with a dummied first entry. Accepting a selectively disclosed ACDC depends on that reading, which rests on an example, so it is graded SHOULD (generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md, A-C1).

reading-compact_v.quote: It provides a regular expression target for determining a serialized field map's serialization format and size (character count), constituting an ACDC message body.
reading-compact_v.inference: Lines 134 to 147 say nothing about the version string's size field in the most compact form, which a presented expanded ACDC does not contain. The generator sizes it to the compact serialization itself, as this sentence says the field gives a serialization's size (generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md, A-B1); accepting an ACDC presented in another form depends on that reading, so it is graded SHOULD.

registry-head.quote: The prior event SAID, `p` field value MUST be the SAID, `d` field value of the immediately prior event in the TEL.
registry-head.inference: The registry's head is fixed by the chain rules for updates, which bind the issuer that writes them, so that a validator should report exactly this head is inferred and graded SHOULD (docs/design.md, ACDC, Registry state).

ts-code.quote: A group consists of its count code followed by one or more Blinded attribute blocks, where each block is composed of a concatenation of the four fields serialized in order as CESR primitives that are appropriate for the BLID, UUID, ACDC SAID, and transaction state string fields in that block.
ts-code.inference: The text fixes the code of a state value only for the empty placeholder (line 2087), so the generator writes states as Tag primitives, as keripy does (generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md, A-B3). The reported state ts depends on that choice, so the head's facts are graded SHOULD.

expand-block.quote: First, expand a given block, verify its SAID, expand its enclosed blocks, verify their SAIDs, and so on as deep as needed or until the leaves are reached.
expand-block.why: Line 136 says to verify by first expanding "a given block" without saying block-level, which could be read as verifying the top-level SAID over the expanded form. The cases follow the keyworded lines 134 and 142, under which the SAID is taken over the most compact form (generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md, A-C3).

aggregate-concat.quote: The baseline standard approach is that the Aggregate field value is a cryptographic digest of the concatenation of an ordered set of the SAIDs of blinded Attribute sub-blocks.
aggregate-concat.why: Line 110 describes the aggregate as a digest of the concatenated SAIDs; line 714 and the worked example at lines 951 to 956 serialize the list with a dummied first entry. The cases follow line 714 and the example (generators/SPEC-ISSUES.md, A-C1).
